newsitem.title: GERMANY: Palm - nations must qualify for EMU without tricks.
newsitem.headline: Palm - nations must qualify for EMU without tricks.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Guntram Palm said on Tuesday that nations must not use tricks but rather step up bonafide efforts to consolidate their finances to qualify for membership of European monetary union.

"He recommended that all Treaty partners stick to the convergence criteria without resorting to tricks," according to a statement from the state central bank of Baden-Wuerttemberg summarising a speech Palm was due to deliver at a conference in Ludwigsburg. Since Germany would miss both the three percent budget deficit criteria and the 60 percent debt criteria this year, policitians at all levels of government should strive to meet the target in 1997, Palm said according to the statement.
The Maastricht Treaty on European union states that nations' budget deficits and government debt must not exceed three percent and 60 percent of GDP respectively.
Political leaders will determine in 1998 which nations will be eligible to join the union after reviewing their 1997 economic data.

Palm also urged nations to adopt the so-called stability pact, designed by German finance minister Theo Waigel to ensure lasting stability within the currency union by imposing fines on EMU nations that fail to maintain fiscal discipline.

Palm, president of the state central bank in Baden-Wuerttemberg, said that Europe's currency union presented a great opportunity for the region but added that it would not singlehandedly solve all of Europe's problems.

While the currency union does not guarantee greater political integration immediately, Palm said that giving up the idea of a currency union would make all further political integration impossible for a number of years to come.
